text: This is what the LORD says: Go down to the house of the king of Judah and speak this word there.
Say: Hear the word of the LORD, king of Judah, you who sit on David's throne—you, your servants, and your people who come through these gates.

This is what the LORD says: Do justice and righteousness. Rescue the one who has been robbed from the hand of his oppressor. Do not wrong or violate the foreigner, the orphan, or the widow, and do not shed innocent blood in this place.
For if you truly do what I have said, then kings who sit on David's throne will come riding through the gates of this house in chariots and on horses—each king with his servants and his people.

versions.text: For if you truly obey this word, then kings who sit on David's throne will come riding through the gates of this house in chariots and on horses—they, their servants, and their people.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew verb is the emphatic infinitive of עשה, "do" (carry out the command of v.3), not "obey a word." Also the closing pronouns are singular in Hebrew ("he, his servants, and his people"), referring to the individual king; the plural "they, their" blurs this.

text: But if you will not listen to these words, I swear by myself, declares the LORD, that this house will become a ruin.
For this is what the LORD says concerning the house of the king of Judah: You are like Gilead to me, like the summit of Lebanon—yet I will surely make you a wasteland, cities without inhabitants.
I will appoint destroyers against you, each with his weapons; they will cut down your finest cedars and throw them on the fire.
Many nations will pass by this city and ask one another, "Why has the LORD done this to such a great city?"
And they will answer: "Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them."

versions.text: And the answer will come: "Because they abandoned the covenant of the LORD their God and bowed down to other gods and served them."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is simply "and they will say," continuing the speech of the passing nations from v.8. "The answer will come" is a vaguer, impersonal paraphrase that obscures who is speaking.

text: Do not weep for the dead or mourn for him. Weep bitterly for the one who goes away, for he will never return to see the land of his birth.
For this is what the LORD says about Shallum son of Josiah, king of Judah, who reigned in place of his father Josiah: He has gone out from this place and will never return.
He will die in the place where they have taken him captive; he will never see this land again.
Woe to him who builds his house by unrighteousness and his upper rooms by injustice, who makes his neighbor work for nothing and does not pay him his wages,
who says, "I will build myself a spacious house with airy upper rooms," who cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it red with vermilion.

versions.text: who says, "I will build myself a spacious house with airy upper rooms," who cuts out windows for it, panels it with cedar, and paints it in vermilion.
versions.explanation: "Paints it in vermilion" is awkward English; the preposition בַּ here is instrumental, so "paints it with vermilion" (or "paints it red with vermilion") reads more naturally aloud.

text: Are you a king because you outdo others in cedar? Did not your father eat and drink, and also do justice and righteousness? Then all went well for him.

versions.text: Does it make you a king to surround yourself with cedar? Your father ate and drank, but he did justice and righteousness, and all went well for him.
versions.explanation: מְתַחֲרֶה means "compete, vie, outdo," which the paraphrase "surround yourself with cedar" loses. The second clause is a rhetorical question in Hebrew (הֲלוֹא), and "but he did justice" wrongly implies a contrast with eating and drinking rather than an addition.

text: He defended the cause of the poor and needy, and it went well for him. Is that not what it means to know me? declares the LORD.
But your eyes and your heart are set on nothing but your own gain—on shedding innocent blood, on oppression and violence.

Therefore this is what the LORD says about Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah: They will not mourn for him, crying, "Alas, my brother! Alas, my sister!" They will not mourn for him, crying, "Alas, my lord! Alas, his majesty!"
He will have the burial of a donkey—dragged away and thrown out beyond the gates of Jerusalem.
Go up to Lebanon and cry out; raise your voice in Bashan; cry out from Abarim, for all your lovers are crushed.
I spoke to you in your prosperity, but you said, "I will not listen." This has been your way since your youth: you have never obeyed my voice.
The wind will shepherd away all your shepherds, and your lovers will go into captivity. Then you will be ashamed and humiliated because of all your wickedness.
You who dwell in Lebanon, nested among the cedars: how you will groan when the pains come upon you, anguish like a woman in labor!
As surely as I live, declares the LORD, even if Coniah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, were a signet ring on my right hand, I would tear you off.
I will hand you over to those who seek your life, to those you dread—to Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon and to the Chaldeans.
I will hurl you and the mother who bore you into another land, where neither of you was born, and there you will die.
To the land they long with all their heart to return to, they will never return.
Is this man Coniah a broken pot, despised and shattered, a vessel no one wants? Why are he and his children hurled out and cast into a land they do not know?
O land, land, land, hear the word of the LORD!
This is what the LORD says: Record this man as childless, a man who will not prosper in his days; for none of his offspring will succeed in sitting on David's throne or ruling again in Judah.
